sugestoes.texto: A missing `refresh_token` is replaced with the placeholder string "refresh_token" in all modes. Office365 Calendar spreads `tokenResponse.data` over the stored credentials, and Microsoft often omits the refresh token, so the real refresh token is overwritten with the literal placeholder and the next refresh fails. Apply the placeholder only in sync mode, or leave the field undefined so the existing token is kept.

`parseRefreshTokenResponse` returns a SafeParse result (`{success, data}`), but it is assigned to `key` and written to `prisma.credential.update`. This stores `{success: true, data: {...}}` as the credential key, so later `googleCredentialSchema.parse(credential.key)` fails. Use `.data` from the result.

The sync branch returns the raw fetch `Response`, while the non-sync branch returns provider-specific shapes. Google and Zoho read `.data`, Hubspot expects a parsed token object, and Lark/Office365/Zoom/Webex/Teams expect specific response handling. Callers therefore receive an incompatible value (`token` is undefined in Google, `hubspotRefreshToken.expiresIn` is undefined, and so on) whenever sync is enabled. The helper also sends no credential or secret to the endpoint and has no timeout. Normalize the sync response (for example `await response.json()`) and adapt it to each caller's expected shape.

`credentialId` (the credential row id) is passed as the third argument, which `refreshOAuthTokens` treats as the Cal.com `userId`. In sync mode the endpoint is asked for tokens of the wrong user (the user whose id equals the credential id). Pass the credential's `userId` instead, which requires threading `credential.userId` into `refreshAccessToken`.

`prisma` is used in this block but is not imported in this file (I grepped and found only line 96). It also calls the Salesforce token endpoint on every `getClient` call without an expiry check and bypasses `refreshOAuthTokens`. The refreshed `accessTokenParsed.data.access_token` is then ignored when building the `jsforce.Connection`, which still uses the stale `credentialKey.access_token`. Import `prisma`, refresh only when expired, route the call through `refreshOAuthTokens`, and use the new access token for the connection.

The webhook secret is compared with `!==`, which is not constant-time and leaks timing information about the secret. This endpoint writes arbitrary credentials for any user, so a successful guess is high impact. Compare with `crypto.timingSafeEqual` on equal-length buffers.

`parseRefreshTokenResponse` returns a SafeParse result (`{success, data}`), but it is assigned to `key` and written to `prisma.credential.update`. This stores `{success: true, data: {...}}` as the credential key, so later `googleCredentialSchema.parse(credential.key)` fails. Use `.data` from the result.

issues.descricao: The new app-credential webhook checks its shared secret with a plain !== string comparison instead of a constant-time comparison, leaking timing information about the secret.

comentarios.texto: Direct !== comparison of webhook secret leaks via timing attack. Use constant-time comparison (e.g., crypto.timingSafeEqual on hashed/buffered values with length check) instead of `req.headers[...] !== process.env.CALCOM_WEBHOOK_SECRET`.

The webhook authenticates a secret using direct string inequality, which is not constant-time and can leak information about the secret through comparison timing. Compare fixed-length representations using a constant-time primitive (such as crypto.timingSafeEqual), handling absent or malformed headers safely, instead of comparing the secret strings directly.

The webhook secret is compared with the `!==` operator, which short-circuits on the first differing byte and leaks the secret via response timing (timing attack). An attacker can iteratively recover CALCOM_WEBHOOK_SECRET and then forge requests that create/update arbitrary user credential keys (decrypted with the AES key) via this endpoint. Use a constant-time comparison, e.g. crypto.timingSafeEqual on equal-length buffers, guarding for length mismatch first.

issues.descricao: The webhook parses the body with zod .parse and decrypts/JSON-parses the keys without error handling, so invalid payloads produce 500 errors instead of 400 responses.
issues.textoGolden: The `appCredentialWebhookRequestBodySchema.parse` function can throw on invalid payloads, resulting in 500 Internal Server Errors instead of the expected 400 Bad Request responses. This can lead to confusion for clients and hinder proper error handling.

comentarios.texto: WHAT: zod parse, symmetricDecrypt and JSON.parse throw unhandled (no try/catch) with no method guard. WHY: Invalid body/keys or GET request crashes handler with 500 and leaks stack, instead of 400/405. HOW: Wrap parse/decrypt in try/catch returning 400 and restrict to POST.

schema .parse plus symmetricDecrypt/JSON.parse throw unhandled (ZodError, decrypt error, SyntaxError) on invalid body or tampered keys, crashing webhook with 500. Use safeParse and try/catch with 400 responses.

issues.descricao: The webhook's non-atomic findFirst-then-create lets concurrent deliveries for the same user and app insert duplicate credential rows.

comentarios.texto: The webhook performs a non-atomic findFirst followed by create when no credential exists. Concurrent deliveries for the same user and app can both observe no row and insert duplicates because Credential has no unique userId/appId constraint; subsequent findFirst updates only one duplicate, leaving competing credentials stale. Serialize the lookup/create operation for each user/app pair or introduce an appropriate uniqueness constraint and atomic upsert.

issues.descricao: parseRefreshTokenResponse writes the hardcoded string 'refresh_token' when the refresh response omits a refresh token, so the stored credential gets an invalid refresh token and later refreshes fail.
issues.textoGolden: The parseRefreshTokenResponse function incorrectly sets refresh_token to the hardcoded string 'refresh_token' when it's missing from the OAuth refresh token response. This invalidates the token, breaking subsequent token refreshes and causing authentication failures.

comentarios.texto: The parser fabricates the literal refresh token "refresh_token" whenever a successful response omits refresh_token, including when synchronization is disabled. Office365's response schema explicitly permits that omission, and its caller merges parsed data over existing credentials, replacing the valid saved refresh token with this invalid value and breaking the next refresh. Leave the property absent so the existing token survives the merge.

When a refresh response omits refresh_token, this helper manufactures the hardcoded credential "refresh_token". Callers such as Office365 merge this into stored credentials, overwriting the valid existing refresh token and causing subsequent provider refreshes to use a predictable invalid token. Leave the field absent and preserve the existing credential when omission is allowed by the provider, or reject the response when a refresh token is required; do not substitute a literal authentication token.

WHAT: Missing refresh_token is replaced with literal string "refresh_token". WHY: Stores bogus refresh token in DB, breaking all future refreshes and masking provider errors. HOW: Preserve existing credential refresh_token or throw instead of injecting placeholder.

issues.descricao: minimumTokenResponseSchema uses computed keys from z.string().toString(), which produce a literal key rather than a wildcard, so the sync-mode schema does not validate or keep expiry and other token fields as intended.
issues.textoGolden: The Zod schema in parseRefreshTokenResponse uses computed property keys [z.string().toString()] and [z.string().optional().toString()] in minimumTokenResponseSchema, which is invalid Zod syntax and will throw a runtime error.

comentarios.texto: `[z.string().toString()]` evaluates to a fixed string key such as "ZodString", so minimumTokenResponseSchema requires a literal numeric property with that name. Every synced token response fails validation and throws "Invalid refreshed tokens were returned". Use `z.object({access_token: z.string()}).passthrough()` instead.

The computed keys `[z.string().toString()]` evaluate to the literal string "[object Object]", not a wildcard. The schema therefore requires a numeric property named "[object Object]", so safeParse always fails in credential-sync mode and the function throws "Invalid refreshed tokens were returned". Use `.passthrough()` on an object with access_token and optional numeric expiry fields instead.

The computed keys `[z.string().toString()]` evaluate to a literal string like "ZodString" and not to a wildcard. The schema therefore requires a numeric property with that nonsense name and never matches real token responses. In sync mode every refresh throws "Invalid refreshed tokens were returned". Use `.passthrough()` and a real expiry check instead.

issues.descricao: In sync mode refreshOAuthTokens returns a raw fetch Response, but callers expect their provider-specific shapes (res.data, axios .data, HubspotToken), so token refresh breaks for Google, Zoho and HubSpot when credential sharing is on.
issues.textoGolden: When APP_CREDENTIAL_SHARING_ENABLED and CALCOM_CREDENTIAL_SYNC_ENDPOINT are set, the refreshFunction helper returns the fetch Response, but several callers (for example GoogleCalendarService.refreshAccessToken expecting res.data, and HubspotCalendarService.refreshAccessToken expecting a HubspotToken) assume it returns the integration-specific token object. That mismatch will cause runtime errors in the sync-enabled path unless the return type or those call sites are adjusted.

comentarios.texto:
WHAT: In the credential-sharing branch `refreshOAuthTokens` returns the raw `fetch` `Response` object instead of a parsed token payload, yet several callers treat the result as an already-parsed token object.
WHY: Callers such as hubspot (`hubspotRefreshToken.expiresIn`), zoho-bigin (`tokenInfo.data.error`), zohocrm (`zohoCrmTokenInfo.data.error`) and googlecalendar (`res?.data`) read `.data`/token fields off the return value; a `Response` has neither, so the sync path yields `undefined`/`NaN` or throws a TypeError — the feature's primary code path is broken for those apps.
HOW: Parse the response (e.g. `const data = await response.json(); return data;`) before returning, or make every caller await the appropriate response handler.

In sharing mode refreshOAuthTokens returns the raw fetch Response (no `.data`), but the google caller reads `res?.data` and then `token.access_token`, throwing a TypeError swallowed by the catch, so the token is never refreshed.

`res?.data` assumes the value returned by refreshOAuthTokens has a `.data` field (true for the `fetchTokens.res` branch), but when APP_CREDENTIAL_SHARING_ENABLED the helper returns a raw `fetch()` Response, which has no `.data`. Then `token.access_token` throws. Either parse the shared-mode Response here or have refreshOAuthTokens return a normalized `{ data }` shape.

issues.descricao: Google Calendar persists the safeParse result object instead of its data as the credential key, corrupting the stored credential so later reads fail.
issues.textoGolden: parseRefreshTokenResponse returns a Zod safeParse result ({ success, data, error }), not the credential key object. Persisting that as key stores the wrapper instead of the token payload; we should store the parsed data or use schema parse.

comentarios.texto: parseRefreshTokenResponse returns a SafeParse result {success,data}, not the parsed key. Storing it directly as `key` writes the wrapper to the credential. Unwrap like other callers: check .success and use .data.

parseRefreshTokenResponse returns SafeParse result {success,data}, but call site stores that wrapper as credential `key` (previously googleCredentialSchema.parse() returned the plain object). Store `key.data` / handle wrapper, otherwise persisted credential becomes {success,data} shape and subsequent credential reads fail.

parseRefreshTokenResponse returns SafeParse wrapper {success,data} but code stores the whole wrapper as credential.key. Office365calendar in same PR unwraps via .data. Persisted credential will be {success,data} instead of tokens, so next load fails validation. Unwrap to .data after success check.

issues.descricao: After switching to parseRefreshTokenResponse, the tokenResponse.success check in Office365 refreshAccessToken is dead code and the previous error logging was dropped.

comentarios.texto: parseRefreshTokenResponse now throws when parsing fails, so the `tokenResponse.success` check on the next line is dead code and the previous error logging was removed. A failed refresh now throws out of refreshAccessToken instead of keeping the old credentials. Catch the error or restore the previous handling.

issues.descricao: Salesforce getClient now refreshes the OAuth token and writes the credential on every service construction, adding a network round trip and DB write even when the access token is valid.

comentarios.texto: getClient now unconditionally exchanges the Salesforce refresh token on every service construction, even when the saved access token is valid. Each constructor invocation adds a blocking OAuth network round trip and credential database write before any Salesforce operation, replacing jsforce's existing on-demand refresh behavior. Keep refresh on demand or guard the exchange with a token-expiration check.

issues.descricao: The new Salesforce token refresh uses prisma without importing it, so the code fails type checking and throws a ReferenceError at runtime.

comentarios.texto: The new credential update references prisma without importing or declaring it; searching this file finds only the new usage. This fails TypeScript checking and raises ReferenceError after a successful token exchange at runtime. Import prisma from @calcom/prisma before using it.

issues.descricao: Zoho Bigin passes the credential id instead of the user id to refreshOAuthTokens, so the sync endpoint receives the wrong calcomUserId.
issues.textoGolden: The `refreshOAuthTokens` function is passed `credentialId` instead of `userId`, which breaks the credential sync functionality by causing incorrect user lookups. This issue can lead to failures in syncing user credentials, impacting user experience.

comentarios.texto:
WHAT: The 3rd argument to `refreshOAuthTokens` is `credentialId` (= `credential.id`, line 53), but the function's parameter is `userId` (`refreshOAuthTokens(refreshFunction, appSlug, userId)`).
WHY: When APP_CREDENTIAL_SHARING_ENABLED, the sync endpoint is sent `calcomUserId: <credential id>` instead of the user id, so Bigin credentials are synced against the wrong/non-existent user (all other apps correctly pass `credential.userId`).
HOW: Pass `credential.userId` instead of `credentialId` as the third argument.

refreshOAuthTokens' third parameter is the Cal.com userId (used as `calcomUserId` in the sync request and to decide whether sharing runs), but this call passes `credentialId`. Every other caller passes `credential.userId`, so the credential-sync endpoint receives a credential row id as the user id and shared credentials are fetched/updated for the wrong identity. Pass `credential.userId` here.

refreshOAuthTokens' third parameter is `userId` (declared in refreshOAuthTokens.ts line 3 and used as `calcomUserId: userId.toString()`), but this call passes `credentialId` (the Credential row id, line 53) instead of the user id. When credential sharing is enabled the customer's sync endpoint receives a credential id labelled as calcomUserId and cannot resolve the correct Cal.com user. Pass `credential.userId` (the BiginToken/credential payload carries it) or plumb the user id through refreshAccessToken.

issues.descricao: Salesforce checks response.statusText !== 'OK' instead of response.ok when refreshing the token, which can misclassify successful responses, and then ignores the refreshed token.
issues.textoGolden: The Salesforce integration checks `response.statusText` instead of `response.ok` when handling OAuth token refresh responses. This can lead to unreliable behavior, as a successful response may not be correctly identified, resulting in the use of stale credentials and potential authentication failures.

comentarios.texto: WHAT: Checks response.statusText !== "OK" instead of response.ok and builds jsforce.Connection from stale credentialKey.access_token/instance_url ignoring accessTokenParsed.data. WHY: Refresh never takes effect (old token reused) and valid refreshes can throw on runtimes where statusText is empty. HOW: Check !response.ok and use parsed access_token/instance_url for connection and DB update.

issues.descricao: After refreshing the Salesforce token, jsforce.Connection is created with the stale access_token and instance_url instead of the newly refreshed values.
issues.textoGolden: The `jsforce.Connection` is created using stale `credentialKey.access_token` and `credentialKey.instance_url` after a token refresh, which can lead to authentication failures and incorrect data access. Ensure that the connection is established using the refreshed token values instead.

comentarios.texto:
WHAT: The new block fetches and persists a fresh access token (`accessTokenParsed.data`) but then creates the `jsforce.Connection` with the stale `credentialKey.access_token` (line 106) instead of the just-refreshed token.
WHY: The refreshed token is written to the DB but never used for the connection; if the old token was expired, jsforce must refresh again (extra round trip) or fail, and the DB/connection state diverge.
HOW: Pass the new access token (`accessTokenParsed.data.access_token`) to the `jsforce.Connection`.

issues.descricao: The app-credential webhook looks up appStoreMetadata by app.slug, but the map is keyed by dirName, so apps whose slug differs from their directory (e.g. google-calendar) always get a 404 and their credentials cannot be synced.

sugestoes.texto: `execute(...)[0]['id']` raises NoMethodError on nil when no `embed_category` row exists, which is the default. The same applies to the `uncategorized_category_id` lookup if that row is absent. This aborts the migration. Use `.first`/`.cmd_tuples` guards and fall back to `Category.where(id: ...)`/a default id when no row is returned.

Legacy `embeddable_hosts` lines are inserted verbatim by raw SQL, so `http://`, `https://` and path parts are kept. The model only strips them in `before_validation`, which raw inserts skip, and `host_allowed?` compares against `uri.host`. Migrated hosts such as `https://example.com` therefore never match and embedding silently stops after upgrade. Normalize each host (strip scheme, path and whitespace, skip blanks) and quote it with `ActiveRecord::Base.connection.quote` before inserting.
The query compares `lower(host)` with `uri.host` without downcasing it. A referer with a mixed-case hostname is rejected even though the host is configured. Use `host.downcase` in the bind value.

`self.host.sub!` is called on a possibly nil host. When the admin controller receives no `host` param, validation raises NoMethodError and returns a 500 instead of a validation error. Guard with `return if host.blank?`, or use non-destructive `self.host = host.to_s.sub(...)`.

`update` and `destroy` use `.where(id:).first` without a nil check. An unknown or already-deleted id produces NoMethodError and a 500 in `host.destroy` and `save_host`. Use `find_by!` or raise `Discourse::NotFound` when the record is missing.

The `*_ids` branch calls `obj[k].map` without checking for an array. A null or non-array `*_ids` attribute in any `__rest_serializer` payload throws and breaks hydration. The `|| []` fallback is dead because `map` always returns an array. Guard with `Array.isArray(obj[k])` and filter out unresolved (undefined) entries.

issues.descricao: EmbeddableHost's before_validation calls self.host.sub! unconditionally, so saving a record with a nil host raises NoMethodError instead of returning a validation error.
issues.textoGolden: The EmbeddableHost model's before_validation callback calls self.host.sub! to strip http://, https://, and path segments, but if self.host is nil, this raises NoMethodError.

comentarios.texto: The before_validation callback calls `sub!` on host without guarding nil. Creating a host with a missing or null host field reaches this callback from save_host and raises NoMethodError instead of returning a validation error. Guard nil during normalization and let presence/format validation reject it.

WHAT: `before_validation` calls `self.host.sub!(...)` unconditionally, so a record with a nil host raises NoMethodError (`nil.sub!`) instead of producing a normal format-invalid result. WHY: `Admin::EmbeddableHostsController#save_host` assigns `params[:embeddable_host][:host]` directly; any request that omits the host value makes the save raise a 500 instead of returning the `render_json_error(host)` validation response. HOW: guard the mutation, e.g. `return if host.blank?` at the top of the before_validation block (or use `self.host = self.host.to_s` before stripping).

before_validation calls self.host.sub!(...) on a possibly-nil host before validates_format_of runs. The controller assigns host.host = params[:embeddable_host][:host], so a request without a host key leaves it nil and nil.sub! raises NoMethodError at save time instead of the format validation producing a normal error response. Add a presence guard so validation reports the failure.

issues.descricao: update and destroy in Admin::EmbeddableHostsController fetch the host with where(id:).first and never check for nil, so an unknown id raises NoMethodError and returns a 500 instead of not-found.
issues.textoGolden: The update and destroy methods in Admin::EmbeddableHostsController do not validate the existence of the EmbeddableHost record retrieved by ID. If EmbeddableHost.where(id: params[:id]).first returns nil (i.e., the host does not exist), attempting to call methods on the nil object (e.g., save_host or destroy) will result in a NoMethodError.

comentarios.texto: In the destroy action, the nil-host case (line 15-16) would raise NoMethodError. Consider adding a nil check to handle the case where the host is not found.

update and destroy fetch the record with EmbeddableHost.where(id: params[:id]).first but never check for nil, then immediately use it (save_host(host) does host.host = ... / host.save; destroy does host.destroy). A stale or already-deleted id, or an interleaving where a concurrent delete removes the row first, makes host nil and the first call on it raises NoMethodError -> unhandled 500. Guard with a nil/404 check before use.

Update passes the nullable result of where(...).first directly to save_host, which immediately assigns host.host. Updating a nonexistent or concurrently deleted record returns an internal error instead of a not-found response; destroy has the same lookup failure. Use find or explicitly raise a not-found error before dereferencing the lookup result.

issues.descricao: record_for_host compares lower(host) against the un-lowercased URI host, so mixed-case referer hosts fail to match allowed hosts and embedding is rejected.
issues.textoGolden: record_for_host compares lower(host) = ? but does not normalize the parameter’s case, so mixed‑case referer hosts may fail to match even though comparison intends to be case‑insensitive.

comentarios.texto: Normalize the parsed hostname before comparing it with lower(host). URI parsing preserves hostname case, so an allowed entry such as example.com does not match https://EXAMPLE.com/page even though DNS hostnames are case-insensitive. This makes valid embedding requests fail the host authorization check and makes category lookup inconsistent for equivalent domain identities. Compare against host.downcase (or normalize both operands equivalently), and add a mixed-case URL test.

The query compares lower(host) to the un-downcased uri.host. A referer such as http://EvilTrout.com never matches the stored lowercase host, so embedding is wrongly denied. Fix: use where("lower(host) = ?", host.downcase).

The query compares lower(host) in the database with uri.host, which is not lowercased, so the comparison normalizes only one side. A referer or URL with uppercase letters (e.g. http://EvilTrout.com) will not match the stored host. Compare against host.downcase, i.e. where('lower(host) = ?', host.downcase).

issues.descricao: The migration copies the legacy embeddable_hosts values into the new table without stripping scheme and path, so hosts stored as http://example.com no longer match the bare-host lookup and previously allowed embeds are rejected after upgrade.
issues.textoGolden: Because this migration inserts embeddable_hosts rows with raw SQL, any existing embeddable_hosts values that include http:// or /https:// or path segments won’t go through the EmbeddableHost model’s normalization, so the new host lookup (which compares only the bare host) may fail for migrated data. Consider ensuring that migrated hosts are normalized to the same format as newly created EmbeddableHost records so existing embedding configurations keep working.

comentarios.texto: WHAT: migration inserts raw embeddable_hosts lines (e.g. http://example.com/123) without stripping scheme/path like the model does. WHY: migrated rows never match EmbeddableHost.record_for_host which compares bare uri.host, silently breaking previously allowed embeds.

Migration INSERTs raw embeddable_hosts lines with scheme/path intact, but EmbeddableHost normalizes to bare domain (before_validation strips protocol/path, record_for_host looks up by URI.host). Strip protocol and path before INSERT or migrated hosts will never satisfy host_allowed?.

Legacy hosts are inserted verbatim instead of applying the new model's scheme/path normalization. Existing values such as http://discourse.org or https://example.com/1234 remain in the table, while record_for_host compares only URI.host, so previously configured embedding hosts stop working after upgrade. Normalize migrated entries to the same representation used by the model before inserting them.

issues.descricao: The contents of category_fabricator.rb and embeddable_host_fabricator.rb are swapped, so each file defines the other's fabricators.
issues.textoGolden: The contents of `category_fabricator.rb` and `embeddable_host_fabricator.rb` have been swapped, resulting in the loss of original category fabricators and potentially causing errors in fabricator usage.

comentarios.texto: File named category_fabricator.rb now defines Fabricator(:embeddable_host) while Fabricator(:category) was moved to embeddable_host_fabricator.rb. Filenames disagree with contents — swap contents back so each file defines the fabricator its name states.

The file names and contents are swapped. embeddable_host_fabricator.rb defines the category fabricators (:category, :diff_category, :happy_category, :private_category), and category_fabricator.rb defines :embeddable_host. Restore category_fabricator.rb to the original category fabricators and put the :embeddable_host fabricator in embeddable_host_fabricator.rb.

issues.descricao: The migration builds its INSERT by interpolating each legacy host value into the SQL string instead of quoting or binding it, so a value with a quote breaks the statement.
issues.textoGolden: The SQL query in the `app/controllers/admin/embeddable_hosts_controller.rb` file uses string interpolation (`'#{h}'`) to insert values, which is vulnerable to SQL injection. It should use parameter binding or proper quoting to prevent this security vulnerability.

comentarios.texto: The migration's INSERT statement uses string interpolation: VALUES ('#{h}', ...). This is a SQL-injection concern and should be fixed by using parameterized queries or proper escaping.
WHAT: migration interpolates raw host string into SQL: VALUES ('#{h}', ...). WHY: a host value containing a single quote breaks the statement and allows SQL injection via site_settings value.

issues.descricao: The migration reads execute(...)[0]['id'] for embed_category without checking for an empty result, so installs without that setting stored crash the migration instead of falling back to the uncategorized category.
issues.textoGolden: The migration accesses execute(...)[0]['id'] without checking if the query returned any rows, which causes a crash when no embed_category setting exists. This can lead to a broken feature when attempting to edit category/host relationships.

comentarios.texto: WHAT: migration does execute(...)[0]['id'] with no guard when embed_category setting/category is missing. WHY: nil[0] dereference crashes the migration and blocks deploy on instances without that setting.
Migration does execute(...)[0]['id'] without checking empty result; missing site_settings row throws NoMethodError and fails migration. Check for nil row.

The migration indexes the first category-query result before checking whether any row was returned. An installation without a persisted embed_category setting, or with no matching category name, aborts migration before reaching the uncategorized fallback. Check whether the result contains a row before accessing its id and handle missing fallback settings as well.

issues.descricao: The spec 'is false if embeddable_host is blank' no longer sets up any host condition and passes only because embed_truncate defaults to false, so its name no longer matches what it tests.

comentarios.texto: Test 'is false if embeddable_host is blank' does not establish the true-branch preconditions (embed_truncate true, has_topic_embed true) nor control host presence, so it passes regardless of host logic and would still pass if host checking were broken/removed. Set truncate true + stub embed true with no hosts for the false case.

The test named "is false if embeddable_host is blank" now uses an ordinary built topic without setting embed_truncate or making has_topic_embed? true. It therefore returns false for reasons unrelated to the missing host, and passes even with the new implementation that never checks host availability. If blank-host behavior remains the intended contract, arrange all the other prerequisites before asserting false; if the contract intentionally changed, replace this case with a test of the actual intended behavior rather than retaining a misleading passing test.

The description "is false if embeddable_host is blank" no longer matches the code. This PR changed Topic#expandable_first_post? (app/models/topic.rb:869) to `SiteSetting.embed_truncate? && has_topic_embed?`, removing the embeddable_hosts condition entirely, and removed the `SiteSetting.embeddable_hosts` setup from this test. The assertion now passes only because `has_topic_embed?` is unstubbed (false) and embed_truncate is unset, so the name states a cause the method no longer has — rename it (e.g. "is false when there is no topic embed") or set up the precondition it claims to test.

issues.descricao: The 'find embedded' test requests fruit 2 but the pretender always returns fruit 1, so it asserts fruit 1's colors and would not notice a find that ignores the id.

comentarios.texto: Test requests fruit id 2 but pretender returns fruits[0] unconditionally, so assertions on colors [1,2] never cover fruit 2's color_ids [3]. Make pretender honor :id or request id 1 / assert single-element case to actually verify plural _ids hydration.

This test now requests fruit 2 but expects fruit 1's two colors. The /fruits/:id Pretender handler always returns fruits[0], so the test passes while hydrating the wrong record and would not catch a find implementation that ignores the requested ID. Make the handler select the requested fruit and assert its ID and corresponding colors (fruit 2 has only color 3), or request fruit 1 if testing its two-color hydration is the goal.

issues.descricao: After saving a host, the component overwrites its category with findById(categoryId); when no category was chosen this is null even though the server saved the uncategorized category, so the row shows no category until reload.

comentarios.texto: The save callback overwrites the category using categoryId even when the server substituted the uncategorized category for a blank selection. Adding a host without choosing a category therefore leaves its category badge empty, and editing it reads an undefined category id despite a valid category_id having been returned. Resolve the category from the saved response's category_id rather than the submitted selection.

When categoryId is null (the default for a new row, or a cleared selection), the controller saves SiteSetting.uncategorized_category_id and returns that category_id. This callback instead overwrites host.category with findById(null), making the displayed category disagree with the saved category. Use the category from the save response or its returned category_id rather than the pre-save selection.

Use the saved response's category rather than overwriting it from categoryId after saving. For a new host with no category selected, categoryId is null, while the new controller deliberately saves SiteSetting.uncategorized_category_id and returns that ID through the serializer. This callback replaces the hydrated category with findById(null), leaving the row without its actual category until reload (and reopening edit also initializes from that incorrect relationship).

issues.descricao: Hosts saved with a port (allowed by the validation regex) are stored as host:port, but lookup compares only URI.host, so those configured hosts never match and embedding fails for them.

comentarios.texto: Host lookup compares URI.host against a stored value that validation explicitly permits to include a port. Saving example.com:8080 succeeds, but a request from http://example.com:8080 produces URI.host equal to example.com and never matches that record, disabling embedding and retrieval for the configured host. Use a consistent port representation in both storage and lookup.

The validator accepts hosts such as `example.com:8080`, but record_for_host extracts only URI.host (`example.com`) and compares it to the stored port-qualified string. An accepted and saved host therefore never authorizes its corresponding URLs. Normalize the stored and queried authority consistently, including a deliberate port policy.

issues.descricao: EmbeddableHost's host format validation only accepts TLDs of 2-5 letters, so admins cannot add embeddable hosts on longer TLDs like example.technology.
record_for_host queries lower(host) on embeddable_hosts, which has no index on host.
The describe block is named allows_embeddable_host but tests host_allowed?.

sugestoes.texto: `<%- end if %>` closes the conditional with a dangling modifier `if` that has no condition. This either raises a syntax error when the template compiles, or wrongly consumes the following ERB code as the condition, so the embed page fails to render. Use `<%- end %>`. The controller spec does not catch this because `TopicView` is stubbed and controller specs don't render views.

`i.content.scrub` is called without a nil check. Feed items with no `content` element (for example summary-only Atom entries) raise NoMethodError, and the exception aborts the loop so no later items are imported. Skip items with blank content, or fall back to `i.description`/`i.summary`. Also guard against a nil `url` and rescue per item so one bad entry doesn't stop the poll.

Imported feed or page HTML is stored as a `raw_html` post without sanitization, and `Post#cook` returns `raw` directly. The `url` is also interpolated unescaped into `<a href='...'>`. Anyone who controls feed or page content can inject `<script>` or event handlers that run on the Discourse origin, both in topics and in the embed iframe (`raw post.cooked`). Sanitize the HTML with a whitelist (for example `Sanitize` or `PrettyText.sanitize`) before storing it, and escape `url` with `ERB::Util.html_escape`.

`discourseUrl.indexOf(e.origin) === -1` is a substring test, so any origin that is a substring of `discourseUrl` (for example `http://foo` against `http://foo.com/`) passes the check. A page on such an origin can send `discourse-resize` messages and control the iframe height. Compare `e.origin` for exact equality with the origin parsed from `discourseUrl`.

issues.descricao: The postMessage handler in embed.js checks the sender with discourseUrl.indexOf(e.origin), a substring test instead of exact origin equality, so a page on an origin that is a substring of the Discourse URL can send forged discourse-resize messages to the embedding page.
issues.textoGolden: The current origin validation using indexOf is insufficient and can be bypassed. An attacker could use a malicious domain like evil-discourseUrl.com to pass this check.

comentarios.texto: The message-origin check uses substring matching: `discourseUrl.indexOf(e.origin) === -1`. Any origin that is a substring of discourseUrl is accepted (e.g. discourseUrl `https://discourse.example.com` accepts origin `https://discourse`), so a malicious page can post `discourse-resize` messages into the embed. Compare against the iframe's actual origin exactly (`e.origin !== expectedOrigin`) instead of a substring test.
Uses indexOf containment instead of origin equality, but it cannot be bypassed.

WHAT: postMessage origin check is reversed (`discourseUrl.indexOf(e.origin)===-1`) instead of strict origin equality. WHY: any e.origin that is a substring of discourseUrl passes, letting a foreign iframe drive `iframe.height` handling and future message branches.

issues.descricao: The referer and embed_url host checks compare against SiteSetting.embeddable_host case-sensitively, so a host differing only in case is rejected even though hostnames are case-insensitive.

comentarios.texto: Host identity is compared case-sensitively: `URI(request.referer).host != SiteSetting.embeddable_host`. Hostnames are case-insensitive, so a referer such as `http://EVILTROUT.COM/...` never matches the configured `eviltrout.com` (and the same flaw exists in lib/topic_retriever.rb:15 for `URI(@embed_url).host`). Normalize both sides with downcase before comparing so case variations of the same host are treated identically.

The referer/host comparison does not lowercase either side, so a mixed-case host is wrongly rejected. The reviewer notes this fails closed and is not a bypass. Normalize case on both sides of the host comparison (e.g. downcase both) to avoid false rejections. The same issue applies to topic_retriever.rb.

The host comparison does not lowercase either side, so a mixed-case host is wrongly rejected. This fails closed and is not a bypass. Normalize case on both sides of the comparison (e.g. downcase both) to avoid false rejections.

issues.descricao: PollFeed reads i.content.scrub for every feed item, so items without a content element (common in RSS feeds that only have description) raise NoMethodError and abort the import of the remaining items.
issues.textoGolden: Calling `i.content.scrub` assumes that `i.content` is always populated. However, many RSS feeds do not provide a `content` field, leading to a potential nil pointer exception when `i.content` is nil. A fallback to `description` should be implemented to prevent crashes.

comentarios.texto: WHAT: `CGI.unescapeHTML(i.content.scrub)` assumes every feed item has a `content` element. WHY: many RSS 2.0 items expose only `<description>` (simple-rss returns nil for `content`), so `nil.scrub` raises NoMethodError and, because the job is `sidekiq_options retry: false`, the entire hourly feed import for all items is aborted. HOW: fall back to the available field, e.g. `(i.content || i.description || i.summary).to_s.scrub`, and skip items whose body is blank.

The feed item is consumed unconditionally: url = i.link, then i.title, and content = CGI.unescapeHTML(i.content.scrub). SimpleRSS item accessors raise NoMethodError when the element is absent (RSS 2.0 feeds frequently carry only <description>, no <content>, and some items have no <link>/<title>), so a single malformed or content-less item aborts the whole hourly job with an unhandled exception instead of skipping it. The code already anticipates a blank link (line 33 fallback) but reads i.content/i.title without a nil guard; use i.content.to_s (or fall back to i.description/summary) and skip items whose content is blank.

`i.content.scrub` raises NoMethodError when a feed item has no content (only a description). The exception aborts the whole poll, so every item after it is never imported. Fall back to `i.content || i.description`, skip items with blank content, and rescue per item.

issues.descricao: Posts imported from RSS or remote pages use cook_method raw_html, which makes Post#cook return the raw HTML without sanitization, and the embed view outputs it with raw post.cooked, allowing stored XSS from imported content.

comentarios.texto: WHAT: the new `return raw if cook_method == Post.cook_methods[:raw_html]` makes `Post#cook` return completely unsanitized HTML, and Jobs::PollFeed stores untrusted feed content this way (poll_feed.rb:35-36 → TopicEmbed.import, unlike import_remote which sanitizes via Readability's tag/attribute whitelist). WHY: the stored `cooked` value is then emitted with `<%= raw post.cooked %>` in app/views/embed/best.html.erb:19, and that page is served from the forum's own origin — so a malicious/compromised RSS feed item containing `<script>` or `onerror=` runs attacker JavaScript in the forum origin and can read cookies/session and perform authenticated actions (stored XSS). HOW: sanitize the raw HTML before persisting it (e.g. run the feed content through the same HTML sanitizer used for regular posts, or restrict the raw_html cook path to trusted, pre-sanitized sources only).

WHAT: Post#cook returns raw verbatim for cook_method raw_html, skipping the cooking/sanitization pipeline and plugin filters. WHY: any RSS/readability HTML imported via TopicEmbed is rendered unsanitized in embed/best.html.erb, executing attacker script in the Discourse origin.

Feed-provided HTML is persisted with raw_html cooking after only Nokogiri parsing and URL rewriting, which do not sanitize scripts or event-handler attributes. A malicious feed entry containing executable HTML is stored as post.cooked and executed under the forum origin when rendered, including through the new raw cooked embed view. Sanitize imported HTML with an explicit safe tag, attribute and URL-scheme allowlist before storing it or returning it from the raw_html cooking path.

issues.descricao: TopicEmbed.import appends a footer that interpolates the URL unescaped into an <a href='...'> tag in raw HTML that is later rendered unsanitized, so a crafted URL can inject markup; it also appends to contents with << without handling nil.
issues.textoGolden: The TopicEmbed.import method is susceptible to a NoMethodError if the contents parameter is nil when attempting to append a string, and an XSS vulnerability due to unescaped url interpolation in the generated HTML.

comentarios.texto: WHAT: TopicEmbed.import interpolates feed-controlled url unescaped into raw HTML (`#{url}`) and stores feed HTML as raw_html. WHY: url passing /^https?\:\/\// can still contain `'`, `>` or script, and RSS content is never sanitized, giving stored XSS when rendered via `raw post.cooked`. HOW: HTML-escape url and sanitize content instead of raw_html passthrough.

TopicEmbed.import interpolates feed-controlled url unescaped into HTML link stored with cook_method raw_html (Post#cook returns raw, bypassing pipeline) and rendered with raw post.cooked: XSS via quote/script break-out. Escape url for text and attribute contexts before storing.

The url is interpolated unescaped into `#{url}`. The post is stored with cook_method raw_html and rendered with `raw post.cooked`, so a url containing a quote or markup is output as live HTML. Escape it with ERB::Util.html_escape (or CGI.escapeHTML) for both the href and the link text.

issues.descricao: TopicEmbed.import appends the footer with contents <<, mutating the caller's string in place instead of building a new string.

comentarios.texto: `contents <<` mutates the caller's string in place. This raises FrozenError for frozen strings and appends the footer twice if the same string is imported again. Use `contents = contents + ...` instead.

issues.descricao: TopicEmbed.import checks for an existing embed and then creates the post and TopicEmbed without handling the unique-index conflict, so two concurrent imports of the same URL make one job fail with RecordNotUnique.

comentarios.texto: TopicEmbed.import does a check-then-insert on embed_url (where(...).first, then TopicEmbed.create!) with no rescue for the unique index declared on topic_embeds.embed_url. The only guard against concurrent intake is the Redis throttle in TopicRetriever, which is bypassed for staff (retrieve_topic.rb:17 passes no_throttle: user.try(:staff?)) and can expire while a slow retrieval (which may synchronously run a full PollFeed, topic_retriever.rb:41) is still running. Two interleaved retrievals for the same URL both see embed.blank? and both attempt creation; the loser raises ActiveRecord::RecordNotUnique, which is unhandled anywhere in the job path, breaking execution. Guard the create against the race (rescue/retry on RecordNotUnique, or use find_or_create_by on embed_url inside the transaction) so concurrent retrievals cannot raise.

Make creation idempotent under concurrent imports. Two workers can both read no embed at line 15 and create posts before attempting the same unique embed_url insert. The unique index correctly rolls back the losing transaction, but its unhandled uniqueness exception aborts that job (and potentially the rest of a feed polling run). This is reachable when scheduled polling overlaps retrieval-triggered polling; the per-URL retrieval throttle does not serialize those paths. Handle the conflict outside the transaction and return the winning embed/post, or serialize imports for the URL.

Race on check-then-create: two concurrent imports both see TopicEmbed.where(embed_url:url).first blank, both create Post + TopicEmbed.create!. Unique index on embed_url then raises RecordNotUnique (unhandled) or creates duplicates. Need atomic find-or-create / rescue unique violation.

issues.descricao: When the embedded post has been deleted, TopicEmbed.import's update path passes a nil embed.post to PostRevisor and crashes on every later import of that URL.

comentarios.texto: On the update path `embed.post` can be nil if the post was deleted. `PostRevisor.new(nil)` then raises NoMethodError, and every later import of that URL fails the same way. Guard against a nil post, for example by skipping the revision or recreating the topic.

WHAT: update path uses `embed.post` without nil guard then `PostRevisor.new(post)`. WHY: if the first post was deleted, post is nil and revise! dereferences nil, crashing feed-poll updates instead of recreating/skipping.

Orphan-post crash on update path: post = embed.post can be nil if the post/topic was deleted, then PostRevisor.new(nil).revise! raises NoMethodError. Must handle missing post (recreate or skip) instead of assuming present.

issues.descricao: Claims import_remote crashes on unparseable pages (nil content) and dead URLs because it does no nil check or network error handling around open(url).read.

comentarios.texto: WHAT: import_remote passes `doc.content` (and title) directly to import where `contents <<` assumes a String, with no nil check or network-error handling around `open(url).read`. WHY: unparseable pages (nil content) raise NoMethodError and dead URLs raise OpenURI errors, crashing RetrieveTopic/Disqus imports with no topic created.

issues.descricao: absolutize_urls only handles root-relative paths: protocol-relative URLs like //cdn.example.com/x.png are rewritten to http://host/cdn.example.com/x.png and path-relative links are left unresolved, breaking links and images in imported posts.

comentarios.texto: The URL rewrite treats protocol-relative URLs such as `//cdn.example.com/image.jpg` as paths on the article host, producing `http://article-host/cdn.example.com/image.jpg`. Imported images and links using protocol-relative external URLs therefore point to the wrong server. Resolve both href and src using URI joining against the article URL, which also handles ordinary relative paths correctly.

Resolve relative href/src references with URI joining rather than handling only leading slashes. For an article at http://example.com/blog/article, href='next' and src='images/photo.jpg' remain relative and resolve against the forum instead of the imported article. Moreover, '//cdn.example.com/photo.jpg' is rewritten to 'http://example.com/cdn.example.com/photo.jpg'. Both yield incorrect links/images in imported posts; apply proper URI resolution to both anchors and images.

absolutize_urls treats any href or src starting with '/' as site-relative and strips all leading slashes. Protocol-relative URLs like '//cdn.example.com/a.png' are rewritten to 'http://site/cdn.example.com/a.png', which is broken. Skip values starting with '//' (or prefix them with the scheme) and only rewrite single-slash paths.

issues.descricao: The embed view formats post dates with a hard-coded strftime pattern, so users in non-English locales see English month names and a fixed order while the rest of the view is translated.

comentarios.texto: The post date uses a hard-coded strftime format `"%e %b %Y"`. `%b` emits English month abbreviations (Jan, Feb, ...) no matter what locale the viewer is in, so the date is frozen to en-US while the surrounding strings in this same view are localized via I18n.t. This is a locale-pinned user-facing format; it should be localized (e.g. via the app's localized date helper / l( ) rather than a literal strftime pattern).

Use a localized date formatter rather than strftime("%e %b %Y"). %b produces English month abbreviations and the fixed day-month-year order ignores the selected locale, although the neighbouring header and footer labels are translated. Embedded comments therefore show English-formatted dates for users of other locales.
Date uses strftime("%e %b %Y") hard-coding one locale's month names/order while neighbouring strings go through I18n.t. Use I18n.l with a locale date format so non-English users see localized dates.

issues.descricao: The Disqus importer now creates topics through TopicEmbed.import_remote, dropping the thread's created_at and the category option and requiring a live HTTP fetch per thread, so imported topics get wrong dates/categories and a dead link aborts the import.

comentarios.texto: WHAT: Disqus import replaced PostCreator (title/raw/created_at/category) with `TopicEmbed.import_remote` per thread, dropping category_id, created_at, and strip handling. WHY: imported topics lose categories/timestamps and now require a live HTTP fetch per thread, failing when links are dead.

Preserve the Disqus thread creation timestamp when switching to TopicEmbed.import_remote. The previous PostCreator call passed `created_at: Date.parse(t[:created_at])`, but this replacement passes only the title, and TopicEmbed.import_remote/import never forward a timestamp to PostCreator. Imported historical topics now get the migration time as their initial post creation date while their replies retain historical dates, losing the importer's chronological fidelity. Extend the import options to forward created_at and pass the thread timestamp here.

The Disqus import now calls TopicEmbed.import_remote instead of PostCreator. This silently drops the `--category` option and the `created_at` from the Disqus thread, and the `--category` method_option was removed from the CLI. It also now makes a live HTTP fetch of every thread link, and `open(url)` raises on a failure that previously could not happen, aborting the whole import. Keep the category and date handling, and rescue fetch errors per thread.

issues.descricao: Every retrieval of an article not yet embedded synchronously polls and imports the entire RSS feed, and since throttling is per URL, many different article requests repeat the full feed download and processing.

comentarios.texto: Every uncached article retrieval synchronously downloads and processes the complete configured feed before fetching the article. Because the retrieval throttle is keyed by individual embed URL, simultaneous requests for different articles each repeat the feed download and all per-item database lookups/imports, multiplying worker load by the number of requests times feed size. Coalesce feed polling with a feed-wide throttle or lock and reuse its recent results instead of executing a full poll per article.

issues.descricao: The 'is 404 without an embed_url' spec never sets an embeddable host, so the request is rejected by ensure_embeddable before the embed_url check runs, and the test would pass even without that check.

comentarios.texto: The test is named 'is 404 without an embed_url' but passes for the wrong reason: it never sets embeddable_host, which defaults to '' so the before_filter `ensure_embeddable` raises at the blank-host check before `params.require(:embed_url)` is reached. The request is rejected regardless of whether the embed_url requirement exists, so the test would still pass if that requirement were removed. Stub a valid embeddable_host here so the failure is actually attributable to the missing embed_url.

The missing-embed_url test does not establish a valid embeddable host and referer, so ensure_embeddable rejects this request before best reaches params.require(:embed_url). It also only checks non-success despite claiming a 404. Removing the required-parameter check would therefore leave this test green. Configure an allowed host/referer for this case and assert the intended missing-parameter response.

The 'is 404 without an embed_url' test never sets embeddable_host, so ensure_embeddable rejects the request before params.require(:embed_url) runs. It passes without the embed_url check. Stub embeddable_host and the referer so the missing param is the only failure cause.

issues.descricao: The 'requires feed_polling_url' and 'requires embed_by_username' specs leave feed_polling_enabled at its false default, so they never reach the condition they name and would pass with those checks deleted.

comentarios.texto: The three 'requires ...' tests do not isolate the guard they name: each stubs only one setting to falsy while the other two remain falsy by default, so poll_feed is never called even if the named check were deleted. Stub the other two settings to truthy values in each test so removing the named guard would cause poll_feed to run and fail the test.

These two tests do not verify the conditions they name. `execute` is guarded by `feed_polling_enabled? && feed_polling_url.present? && embed_by_username.present?`, and feed_polling_enabled defaults to false. Neither test stubs feed_polling_enabled? to true, so the guard short-circuits at the first clause and poll_feed is never called no matter what feed_polling_url/embed_by_username are. Both would still pass if the URL/username checks were deleted entirely. Stub `SiteSetting.stubs(:feed_polling_enabled?).returns(true)` in each so the specific condition under test is actually reached.

The URL and username prerequisite tests never enable feed polling (whose configured default is false) or supply the other required setting. execute consequently short-circuits at feed_polling_enabled? and never evaluates the prerequisite each test claims to cover. Both tests still pass if their corresponding presence checks are removed. Set all other prerequisites to valid values before making only the setting under test absent, so the poll_feed.never expectation actually detects removal of that guard.

issues.descricao: PollFeed.feed_key computes a per-feed cache key that is never used, so the feed is re-fetched and re-processed every hour without a modified-since check.
The embed layout references the 'embed' stylesheet and embed.js, but neither is in config.assets.precompile, so with precompiled assets in production the embed page fails to load them.
The retrieve throttle is keyed by the full embed URL, so an anonymous client can vary the query string on the embeddable host to bypass it and make the server create an unbounded number of topics.

The "requires feed_polling_enabled?" spec leaves feed_polling_url and embed_by_username at their blank defaults, so poll_feed is skipped regardless and the test would pass even without the enabled check.
TopicEmbed.import_remote fetches the embed URL with open(url).read and no timeout or size limit, so a slow or huge remote page can block the background job and exhaust memory.
The retrieve throttle sets the Redis key with setnx and sets its TTL in a separate expire call, so a crash between the two leaves a key without expiry that blocks retrieval of that URL forever.
`import_remote` fetches the embed URL with open-uri, which follows redirects, so the embeddable-host check on the initial URL can be bypassed to reach internal services (SSRF).

sugestoes.texto: The Lithuanian `loginTotpStep1` was replaced with an Italian sentence ("Installa una delle seguenti applicazioni sul tuo cellulare:"). Lithuanian users now see Italian text in the TOTP setup page. The same Italian text was put into `account/messages/messages_lt.properties` `totpStep1`. Replace both with a Lithuanian translation of "Install one of the following applications on your mobile:", or remove the keys so they fall back to English.

The `zh_CN` `totpStep1` was replaced with a Traditional Chinese string ("在您的手機上安裝以下應用程式之一："). Simplified Chinese users now see Traditional characters. Use a Simplified Chinese translation, or remove the key so it falls back to English.

The Lithuanian account `totpStep1` was replaced with an Italian sentence ("Installa una delle seguenti applicazioni sul tuo cellulare:"). Lithuanian users will see Italian text in the account TOTP setup instructions. Replace it with a Lithuanian translation such as "Įdiekite vieną iš šių programėlių savo mobiliajame telefone:", or remove the key so it falls back to English.

issues.descricao: The Lithuanian TOTP setup step was replaced with Italian text in both the account and login bundles.
issues.textoGolden: The translation is in Italian instead of Lithuanian. This should be translated to Lithuanian to match the file's locale (messages_lt.properties).

comentarios.texto: The Lithuanian OTP setup instruction has been replaced with an Italian sentence. login-config-totp.ftl renders this message directly, so users selecting Lithuanian receive an instruction in the wrong language; the same copied sentence also appears in the Lithuanian account bundle at line 101. Replace both values with the Lithuanian translation of the new installation instruction.

The replacement OTP setup instruction is Italian (“Installa una delle seguenti applicazioni sul tuo cellulare”), but this is the Lithuanian locale and the surrounding setup steps are Lithuanian. Translate the new instruction into Lithuanian rather than copying the Italian translation. The same incorrect replacement appears in the login bundle at themes/src/main/resources-community/theme/base/login/messages/messages_lt.properties:71 and should be corrected there too; otherwise Lithuanian users see an untranslated first step in both OTP setup flows.

The replacement OTP setup instruction is Italian, not Lithuanian (`Installa una delle seguenti applicazioni sul tuo cellulare`). Translate both replacements into Lithuanian so selecting Lithuanian does not display Italian instructions during authenticator setup.

issues.descricao: The zh_CN totpStep1 translation is written in Traditional Chinese instead of Simplified Chinese.
issues.textoGolden: The totpStep1 value uses Traditional Chinese terms in the Simplified Chinese file (zh_CN), which is likely incorrect for this locale. Please verify the locale‑appropriate translation.

comentarios.texto: The zh_CN (Simplified Chinese) file was given Traditional Chinese characters: totpStep1=在您的手機上安裝以下應用程式之一：. Compare the unchanged neighbouring lines (e.g. '打开应用扫描二维码…') which use Simplified forms; 手機/應用程式/安裝 are Traditional. zh_CN must be Simplified Chinese, so this string is in the wrong script/variant for the locale.
totpStep1 in messages_zh_CN uses Traditional Chinese (手機, 安裝, 應用程式), not Simplified Chinese as the rest of the file does. Replace it with the Simplified form: 在您的手机上安装以下应用之一：
The Simplified Chinese (zh_CN) totpStep1 was replaced with Traditional Chinese ("在您的手機上安裝以下應用程式之一："). Use the Simplified form, "在您的手机上安装以下应用程序之一：".

issues.descricao: The method santizeAnchors is misspelled; it should be sanitizeAnchors.
issues.textoGolden: The method name 'santizeAnchors' should be 'sanitizeAnchors' (missing 'i').

issues.descricao: HTML_TAGS is a non-static, non-private field instead of a private static final constant.
issues.textoGolden: Field HTML_TAGS should be declared as 'private static final' following Java naming conventions for constants

issues.descricao: The diff-trimming code computes common prefix and suffix independently, so they can overlap and substring throws StringIndexOutOfBoundsException, crashing the verifier instead of reporting the illegal HTML.

comentarios.texto: The common prefix (start) and common suffix (end) are computed independently and can overlap, for example value "aa" vs sanitized "a". Then substring(start, length - end) gets begin > end and throws StringIndexOutOfBoundsException, so the verifier crashes instead of reporting the illegal HTML. Bound the suffix scan so that start + end <= min(value.length(), sanitized.length()), e.g. `while (end < min - start && ...)`.

The common prefix and common suffix are computed independently and can overlap, so `sanitized.substring(start, sanitized.length() - end)` can have start > end and throw StringIndexOutOfBoundsException. This crashes the verifier instead of reporting 'Illegal HTML'. Cap the suffix scan with `end < Math.min(value.length(), sanitized.length()) - start`.

WHAT: Common prefix/suffix stripping for the diff message can compute start+end larger than the string length and call substring(start, length-end) with start > end. WHY: Throws StringIndexOutOfBoundsException inside the key loop and crashes verification instead of reporting Illegal HTML. HOW: Clamp end so start+end <= min lengths, e.g. stop suffix scan when end >= length-start.

comentarios.texto: Choice normalization removes all branch content before HTML validation, allowing prohibited markup to bypass the new translation policy. A translated error-invalid-multivalued-size value such as `{2,choice,0#values|1#value|1

WHAT: normalizeValue replaces the entire {n,choice,...} block with ... before sanitizing, so HTML inside choice options is never checked. WHY: A translation can smuggle tags (e.g. {2,choice,0#<script>...}) in error-invalid-multivalued-size/linkExpirationFormatter keys and pass the verifier, reaching UI rendering as XSS. HOW: Sanitize/validate the choice body instead of blanking it, or run the HTML policy on the inner choice text as well.

issues.descricao: The account and admin UI bundles now use Java MessageFormat placeholders and choice syntax for error-invalid-multivalued-size, but i18next expects {{n}}, so the UI shows literal {0}/{1}/{2} and the raw choice text.

comentarios.texto: The admin-ui bundle is consumed by react-i18next, which interpolates with double-brace `{{0}}` syntax (the previous value was `Attribute {{0}} ... {{2}}`). This line was rewritten to Java MessageFormat/ICU syntax (`{0}` ... `{2,choice,0#values|1#value|1<values}`), which i18next does not understand: the placeholders will not be substituted and the literal `{2,choice,...}` text will be shown to users. Keep the JS-side value in `{{0}}` form (and don't introduce ICU ChoiceFormat into the JS bundle); the ICU/choice spelling belongs only in the Java theme properties.

Same contract break in the account-ui bundle: the value was `Attribute {{0}} must have at least {{1}} and at most {{2}} value(s).` (i18next double-brace interpolation) and was changed to `{0}`/`{2,choice,...}` MessageFormat+ICU syntax. The account console's i18next based consumer was not updated to match, so interpolation will fail and the raw placeholder/choice syntax will be rendered. Restore `{{0}}`-style placeholders for the JS bundle.

The account-ui bundle is consumed by i18next, which interpolates with double braces (the original string was `Attribute {{0}} must have at least {{1}} and at most {{2}} value(s).`). This PR aligned the value to the Java theme convention, replacing `{{0}}/{{1}}/{{2}}` with `{0}/{1}/{2}` and adding ICU `{2,choice,...}`. i18next will no longer substitute the placeholders and cannot interpret the ICU choice, so the account UI shows the raw `{0}`, `{1}`, `{2}` and literal choice text. Keep the JS-side double-brace form for this bundle (adapt the choice accordingly) rather than the Java single-brace/ICU form used by the theme messages.

issues.descricao: If the English counterpart of a messages_*.properties file does not exist, verifySafeHtml throws an unchecked RuntimeException that escapes the mojo, crashing the build instead of reporting a validation message.
The theme verifier's HTML and anchor regexes are case-sensitive, so uppercase tags in translations are flagged as illegal HTML by the build.

The anchor regex </?a[^>]*> in the theme verifier treats any tag starting with 'a' (<abbr>, <area>, ...) as an anchor tag, which can produce misleading anchor errors or strip such tags before HTML sanitizing.
The anchor-mismatch error in VerifyMessageProperties omits the message key and file, so the failing translation is hard to locate, unlike the 'Illegal HTML' message.

sugestoes.texto: `totalPages` uses `Math.floor(user_count / limit) + 1`, which overcounts by one when `user_count` is an exact multiple of `limit` (e.g. 50 members gives 2 pages). On the real last page `showingLast` is false, so Next stays enabled and loads an empty page. Use `Math.ceil(user_count / limit)`.

`add_members` calls `group.add(user)` (`users.push`) for every submitted username without checking whether the user is already a member. Re-adding a current member inserts a duplicate `group_users` row, which most likely raises a unique-index error and returns a 500. The old `usernames=` code diffed against current members, so this is a regression. Skip users already in `group.users`, for example with `group.add(user) unless group.users.exists?(user.id)`, and strip whitespace from each username.

`limit` comes straight from `params[:limit]` with no upper or lower bound, and the old cap for non-automatic groups was removed. A request with a huge limit loads and serializes every member of a large group in one response. A negative limit causes a SQL error. Clamp it, for example `limit = [[(params[:limit] || 50).to_i, 1].max, 200].min`, and clamp `offset` to at least 0.

issues.descricao: The admin group pager computes total pages as floor(user_count / limit) + 1, so when the member count is an exact multiple of the limit it shows an extra page and Next navigates to an empty member list.
issues.textoGolden: The `totalPages` calculation using `Math.floor(user_count / limit) + 1` produces an extra page when `user_count` is an exact multiple of `limit`, leading to incorrect pagination. For example, with 100 users and a limit of 50, it reports 3 pages instead of 2, allowing navigation to an empty page.

comentarios.texto: totalPages (and currentPage) use `Math.floor(user_count / limit) + 1`, which is an off-by-one when user_count is an exact multiple of limit (e.g. 50 members, limit 50 → reports 2 pages although only 1 exists). This leaves `showingLast` false on the real last page, so 'next' navigates to an empty page at offset=user_count. Use `Math.ceil(user_count / limit)` (and compute currentPage consistently) to get the correct page count.

totalPages is off by one when user_count is an exact multiple of limit: `Math.floor(user_count / limit) + 1` gives 2 for user_count=50, limit=50, although 50 members occupy exactly one page. Correct it to `Math.ceil(this.get('user_count') / this.get('limit'))`. Effect: for a group whose member count is a multiple of the page size, totalPages is one too high, showingLast remains false so the 'next' link stays enabled, and clicking it navigates to a phantom empty page.

`totalPages` uses `Math.floor(user_count / limit) + 1`, which over-counts by one whenever `user_count` is an exact multiple of `limit` (e.g. 50 members with limit 50 yields 2 pages instead of 1). Since `showingLast` is `propertyEqual("currentPage", "totalPages")`, on a full last page `showingLast` is false, so the `next` action stays enabled and advances `offset` to `user_count`, rendering an empty page labeled as the last page. Use `Math.ceil(user_count / limit)` (with the zero-member guard) so the count matches the real number of pages.

issues.descricao: Several Group model functions (findMembers, destroy, userCountDisplay) return a value on some paths and undefined on others, triggering consistent-return lint warnings.
issues.textoGolden: Expected to return a value at the end of function - code paths without explicit returns will return undefined

issues.descricao: Paging actions fire overlapping member requests and each response unconditionally overwrites offset and members, so a stale response arriving last can revert the list to an earlier page.

comentarios.texto: Guard against stale member-fetch responses before updating the model. `next` updates offset immediately and leaves navigation enabled, so with at least three pages two rapid clicks issue requests for offsets 50 and 100. If the offset-100 response arrives first and the offset-50 response arrives last, this unconditional `setProperties` resets both offset and members to the older page, undoing the latest navigation. Refreshes after membership changes can similarly be overwritten by an earlier fetch. Track a per-model request generation and apply only the latest response, or serialize navigation and refresh requests.

issues.descricao: The public members endpoint now always caps results at 50 per page, but the public group members page has no pagination, so groups with more than 50 members are silently truncated for users.

comentarios.texto: The public members route now loads only the model's default 50-member page without providing any way to request subsequent pages. The public group/members.hbs template only renders members and has no Next/Previous controls, so members after the first 50 become inaccessible (manual groups previously returned all members). Add public pagination controls and actions that update offset and reload members.

The new default limit applies to nonautomatic groups as well, but the public group-members route still calls findMembers() only once and its template simply iterates members without pagination. Previously this endpoint returned every member of a nonautomatic group; now a group with more than 50 members exposes only the first 50 on its public members page, with no way to reach the rest. Update that consumer to fetch subsequent pages or provide pagination when introducing this endpoint contract.

Provide pagination or load subsequent pages for the public group-members view. findMembers now requests only 50 members, and this route calls it only once while its template simply iterates members without navigation. Custom groups previously returned all members, so groups larger than 50 now have members that cannot be viewed on this page.

issues.descricao: Creating a group ignores the alias_level the admin selected, saving only name and visibility, so new groups keep the default alias level.

comentarios.texto: Persist params[:alias_level] when creating a group, just as update does. The creation form exposes aliasLevelOptions and group.asJSON sends the selected alias_level, but create saves only name and visible. A newly created group therefore retains the default alias level instead of the administrator's selection.

issues.descricao: Removing a member deletes the membership row directly and skips clearing the user's primary_group_id, so a removed user can keep this group as their primary group.

comentarios.texto: WHAT: remove_member uses group.users.delete(user_id) instead of the Group#remove destroy path. WHY: bypasses GroupUser destroy callbacks and primary_group_id cleanup done in destroy_deletions, leaving stale membership side-effects (e.g. dangling primary_group_id). HOW: load the User and call group.remove(user).

Removing a member with group.users.delete bypasses the primary_group_id cleanup previously performed by Group#destroy_deletions during usernames updates. A user whose primary group is this group remains associated with it as their primary group after membership removal, leaving stale primary-group state used by user administration and post serialization. Clear primary_group_id for the removed user when it equals this group's id as part of the removal operation.

issues.descricao: The remove_member spec issues a PUT request although the route only maps DELETE to remove_member, so the test uses a verb never routed in production.
issues.textoGolden: The remove_member test uses xhr :put to call the remove_member action, but the route defines delete 'members' => 'groups#remove_member' requiring DELETE method.

comentarios.texto: This example sends `xhr :put, :remove_member`, but the PR maps `remove_member` only to DELETE (`delete "members" => "groups#remove_member"`); PUT on that path routes to `groups#add_members`. Controller specs bypass the router, so the example still lands on `remove_member` and passes regardless — it would still pass if the DELETE route were missing or wired to the wrong action, leaving the newly introduced verb/action pairing untested. Use `xhr :delete, :remove_member`, as the sibling example at line 125 already does.

The test 'cannot remove members from automatic groups' sends `xhr :put, :remove_member`, but the route is `delete "members" => "groups#remove_member"`. It exercises the action with a verb that is never routed in production. Use `xhr :delete, :remove_member, group_id: 1, user_id: 42` so the test matches the real request.

issues.descricao: Admin add_members pushes every username into group.users without skipping existing members, so adding someone already in the group hits the unique group_users index, returns a 500 and leaves earlier users partially added.
The public group members endpoint takes `limit` from params with no upper bound or positivity check, letting a visitor request huge pages or trigger a 500 with a negative limit.

Admin remove_member deletes memberships with group.users.delete, which skips GroupUser callbacks, so the cached groups.user_count is never decremented and stays inflated.
Group member pagination is off by one when user_count is a multiple of limit: Next moves to offset == user_count and shows an empty page.
`add_members` runs one User query per username; load all users with a single `User.where(username: ...)` query.

sugestoes.texto: `MetricAlertDetectorHandler` extends the abstract `StatefulDetectorHandler` but implements none of its abstract members (`counter_names`, `get_dedupe_value`, `get_group_key_values`, `build_occurrence_and_event_data`). `MetricAlertFire` registers it as `detector_handler`, so `Detector.detector_handler` raises `TypeError: Can't instantiate abstract class` for every `metric_alert_fire` detector. Implement the abstract methods, or keep a concrete `evaluate` that returns `{}` until the stateful handler is built.

`MetricAlertDetectorHandler` extends the abstract `StatefulDetectorHandler` but implements none of its abstract methods (`get_dedupe_value`, `get_group_key_values`, `build_occurrence_and_event_data`, and any other abstract members such as `counter_names`). issues.textoGolden: MetricAlertDetectorHandler inherits from StatefulDetectorHandler but only contains pass, failing to implement its required abstract methods: counter_names (property), get_dedupe_value(), get_group_key_values(), and build_occurrence_and_event_data().
